title: The Unsent, First Bloom in the Row
statement: Sunny keeps a chart of flowers and the plantation had none. The tallest of Tessera's six cores, the one cut deepest, has opened a small pale bloom at its top, and it faces left, back toward the vessel it was taken from, the way anything that has been cut from something turns toward it in the light. The flower is four petals of pale light and a centre the colour of the wood. The other five cores stay as shoots. I added nothing else, because a row with one flower in it is already louder than I like. Sunny's chart says four. The next hand can let the others follow, or pick this one.
process: I kept Tessera's parent entirely, the scarred vessel, the six core strips, their roots and shoots, and added a single bloom at the top of the tallest strip: a short stem curving left, a soft halo and four petal ellipses of pale light with a small wood-coloured centre. Nothing else was changed.

proposal.direction: Let the tallest of the six cores flower first: a small pale bloom at its top, the other five still shoots, and the flower facing the vessel it was cut from.
proposal.rationale: Three flowers in fifty-seven works; she keeps a chart, and the room agreed that a plantation with nothing in bloom is only a fence.
